questions.q: Why does the security engineering team choose to federate Entra ID and Okta first, rather than migrating every Thornbury app to Entra ID on day one of the merger?
options: Okta cannot be decommissioned under any circumstances
Federation is required by law whenever two companies merge
Entra ID does not support SAML or OIDC applications
Federation lets Thornbury's ~40 apps migrate on their own schedule over two quarters instead of all at once, avoiding an outage risk for no urgent gain
questions.explain: Forcing every app onto the same day-one timeline risks real login outages; federating first lets Entra ID become the surviving identity plane while apps cut over gradually.

questions.q: What specifically makes PolicyTrack's migration different from ClaimLine's?
options: PolicyTrack only supports SAML 2.0 and has a signing certificate expiring in seven months, while ClaimLine uses OIDC and needs a new client ID and redirect URI
PolicyTrack and ClaimLine both use the exact same SSO standard and migration steps
ClaimLine cannot be integrated with Entra ID under any circumstances
PolicyTrack has no users and does not need to be migrated
questions.explain: The SSO standard each app uses determines the migration work: SAML needs a new entity ID/ACS URL, OIDC needs a new client ID/redirect URI.

questions.q: Why is the MFA rollout split into three phases instead of one immediate cutover for all of Thornbury's users?
options: Phased rollouts are slower for no reason and add no safety benefit
Microsoft Entra ID cannot support more than one MFA method at a time
FIDO2 hardware keys cannot be issued to more than one department per month
Castellan and Thornbury started from very different places — Thornbury had no Conditional Access and 60% of users on SMS, so the rollout has to meet them where they are before raising the bar
questions.explain: A phased rollout — pilot, then full standard-user cutover, then admin hardware keys — accounts for the real gap between where each org started.

questions.q: What does running a report-only Conditional Access policy during Phase 1 of the MFA rollout accomplish?
options: It has no effect and is only used for documentation
It logs what the policy would block without actually blocking anything yet, surfacing problems before enforcement affects real users
It permanently disables Conditional Access for the pilot group
It immediately blocks every sign-in that doesn't use a FIDO2 key
questions.explain: Report-only mode is the audit-before-enforce discipline this course teaches for any control, catching mistakes before they affect real users.

questions.q: In this lesson's identity plane framing, what role does the surviving identity provider (Entra ID) play once federation begins?
options: It becomes the centralized system other security controls — Conditional Access, SSO, Zero Trust — depend on, even while Okta still brokers some Thornbury apps
It only applies to applications that use OIDC, never SAML
It is replaced entirely by Okta for the duration of the merger
It stops being used for any Castellan employees during the transition
questions.explain: The identity plane is the centralized layer other controls key off of; federating means Entra ID holds that role while Okta remains a downstream broker temporarily.
